title: POC integration design — SDK + OpenAPI endpoints, function-calling, structured output — Sable Systems
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC focused on integrating Redwood's SDK and OpenAPI-compatible endpoints. Agreement on success criteria (latency, throughput, end-to-end accuracy on structured extraction tasks), benchmark plan, and initial timeline. Action items assigned for sandbox access, benchmark dataset, and initial test harness. Follow-up to deliver pricing guardrails and security docs.
topics: deployment mode discussion (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)
action_items: Adrian Patel - Provide starter Redwood SDK examples (Node/Python) + repo link by 2026-11-20
Marcus Li - Share representative QA dataset (5000 records) and baseline latency numbers by 2026-11-22
Priya Singh - Share security questionnaire and SSO requirements by 2026-11-24
Maya Chen - Send sandbox credentials and POC runbook by 2026-11-19
Elena Torres - Confirm success criteria weightings (latency vs accuracy) by 2026-11-23
next_steps: Redwood to provision sandbox with OpenAPI-compatible endpoints and function-calling enabled
Customer to supply sample dataset + expected structured output schema
Redwood to share SOC2 and encryption (KMS) docs and draft pricing estimate for 6-week POC
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Adrian Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CSM) — Sable: Ravi Kumar (CTO), Elena Torres (Lead ML), Marcus Li (Platform), Priya Singh (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — looks like we've got a full house from Sable. Quick intro round, then dive into the POC goals.
[00:10] Ravi: Yeah thanks. We're hoping to validate a drop-in integration path — use your SDKs or OpenAPI-compatible endpoints, exercise function-calling for our internal tools, and validate structured extraction for invoices and receipts.
[00:24] Adrian: Great. From the SE side we'll focus on three measurable axes: latency and throughput for your peak concurrency, token-cost math (rough unit economics), and structured output fidelity against your label set.
[00:36] Elena: When you say structured output fidelity, do you mean exact field mapping? We need JSON schema validated for downstream systems.
[00:45] Maya: Exactly — we want to show that function-calling or structured output templates can produce validated JSON that passes your schema checks at X% accuracy threshold.
[00:54] Marcus: Our baseline is: 95% field-level correctness on the header fields (vendor, date, total) and end-to-end latency below 350ms  p95 when running against our typical batch size — that's our goal but open to tradeoffs.
[01:12] Priya: Also, must confirm security: SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, SOC2 Type II, data residency controls and KMS integration for key management.
[01:23] Maya: Totally understood — we can surface our SOC2, encryption in transit & at rest docs, and we support customer KMS for Private deployments. For hosted sandbox we'll provide temporary keys and logs.
[01:36] Adrian: Quick note on the OpenAPI-compatible endpoints: Redwood offers an OpenAI-API-compatible surface that maps to our runtime with function-calling extensions. For the POC we can enable both SDK and raw OpenAPI endpoints so you can test both flows concurrently.
[01:54] Elena: Good, we want to exercise both. Our platform currently uses an OpenAI-style client library; swapping endpoints should be low-effort if the request/response shape matches.
[02:06] Maya: We'll provide Node and Python SDK snippets that mimic your existing client usage patterns, plus a guide for the alt OpenAPI endpoints. Adrian will push a sample repo.
[02:18] Adrian: I'll include examples for streaming responses, function calling with typed parameters, and structured output enforcement via JSON schema.
[02:28] Ravi: Let's talk workload sizing — our traffic is pretty spiky during end-of-month invoice runs. Normal steady-state is ~20 rps, spike to 250 rps for a 10–15 minute window. Average payload is ~350 tokens per request, some up to 1k.
[02:45] Marcus: Also note we batch internal requests from a queuing layer; so concurrency on the inference endpoint can look like sustained 80–120 concurrent streams during spikes.
[02:53] Adrian: Ok that helps. For the POC we'll create a benchmark harness that simulates your traffic profile: steady 20 rps, then spike windows to 250 rps, paying attention to cold-start behavior and p95 tail latency.
[03:06] Elena: Are you able to simulate KV-cache warmup and prefix caching? A lot of our calls hit similar prefixes so caching matters.
[03:14] Adrian: Yes, we can replay a representative prefix distribution. We'll want your sample dataset so caching accuracy is realistic.
[03:21] Maya: Success criteria proposal: (1) p95 latency < 350ms for 80% of steady-state and <500ms p95 during spikes for critical endpoints; (2) field-level extraction >= 95% for the core invoice schema; (3) cost per 1k tokens within the guardrail we'll share; (4) function-calling reliability > 99% across 1k calls. Thoughts?
[03:42] Ravi: Those look reasonable as initial targets. We may tighten accuracy later. Please add a quality regression test for critical fields.
[03:49] Elena: Also add a test for malformed inputs — we want to ensure structured output validators can handle partial failures and that the API returns consistent error codes.
[03:58] Adrian: We'll include input fuzzing and a schema validation layer in the harness. We'll capture both model failure modes and network/timeout errors.
[04:07] Priya: On the security side — we need audit logs for token usage, per-API-key tracing, and ability to revoke keys. Also, do you support VPC peering or private deployment for PII-heavy data?
[04:18] Maya: For enterprise customers, yes: Private deployment options include VPC/private control plane and integrations with your KMS/HSM. For the hosted POC we can do strict retention policies and access controls. We'll attach details.
[04:30] Marcus: Latency from our region matters — we run in us-west1. Can you place POC endpoints in that region?
[04:36] Adrian: We have hosted endpoints in us-west1; we'll route the POC traffic there. If needed we can also test dedicated capacity in us-west.
[04:45] Maya: Timeline proposal: provision sandbox + repo by 2026-11-19; customer shares datasets by 2026-11-22; benchmark kickoff engineer-to-engineer week of 2026-11-23; first round results by 2026-11-30; iterated tuning and a short second round, final POC review the week of 2026-12-07. That puts the POC at roughly 6 weeks.
[05:06] Ravi: That aligns to our internal windows. We want a go/no-go checkpoint after the first round of benchmarks to decide whether to proceed to dedicated evaluation.
[05:16] Elena: What about model variants & quantization — will you test smaller, cheaper variants for cost tradeoffs?
[05:22] Adrian: Yes, Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings. For the POC we'll test a primary model that matches your accuracy needs, plus one quantized variant to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:33] Marcus: How will you measure cost? We need a per-1k token cost estimate and a framework for amortizing batching savings.
[05:40] Maya: We'll produce a cost report that shows raw token cost, batching impact, and estimated monthly cost at your throughput curve. We'll include sensitivity analysis.
[05:48] Ravi: Good. A couple of integration details: we have existing tools that need to be called by the model (invoice lookup, vendor confidence endpoint). Function-calling should be able to call those services with a consistent contract.
[05:59] Adrian: We'll model function-calling with typed parameters and simulated service stubs in the sandbox. We can also demonstrate fallback behaviors if the function call fails.
[06:09] Elena: We'll need a mapping doc for how function outputs map to your downstream DB schemas.
[06:14] Maya: We'll co-author that mapping artifact; I'll put it in the repo.
[06:19] Priya: Regarding compliance, can you provide attestations around data deletion after the POC, and confirm no model training on customer data?
[06:27] Maya: Redwood does not use customer data to train public models. For hosted POC we'll enforce non-persistent storage options on request and provide deletion certificates when necessary. We'll capture this in the security pack.
[06:39] Marcus: One potential blocker is our procurement approval — we may need a short legal review. Is there a standard MSA or POC agreement?
[06:46] Lena: Yes, we have a POC agreement template we can share; it includes liability caps, IP clauses, and data handling. We'll send it alongside the sandbox.
[06:55] Ravi: About observability — we need request-level traces and token-level cost breakdowns to map back to our billing.
[07:01] Adrian: The Redwood Console exposes per-request traces, model route dashboards, and token-level cost breakdowns. We'll show sample dashboard screenshots in the runbook.
[07:10] Elena: For the structured output validation, can we run an automatic regression every commit? We want the harness to integrate with our CI.
[07:17] Adrian: Yes — the test harness can be run as part of CI; we'll provide a dockerized runner and a small GitHub Action example.
[07:26] Maya: Okay — to recap the concrete next steps: 1) Redwood sends SDK samples, sandbox creds, SOC2 + security docs; 2) Sable sends sample dataset + schema + SSO requirements; 3) schedule engineer-to-engineer benchmark kickoff; 4) Redwood sends POC agreement. Any additions?
[07:42] Ravi: Add the cost guardrails and expected support SLA for the POC (on-call windows).
[07:48] Maya: Noted — we'll include a support contact & on-call SLA for POC windows.
[07:54] Elena: One last question — what happens after POC if we want dedicated capacity? Typical lead time?
[07:59] Maya: Dedicated reservations usually require a negotiation but can be stood up in 2–4 weeks depending on region and capacity. We'll include expected timelines in the pricing doc.
[08:09] Marcus: Great. If we hit the accuracy and latency targets, procurement can start parallel path.
[08:14] Maya: Perfect. We'll follow up with the attachments and the sandbox details tomorrow. Thanks everyone.
[08:20] Ravi: Thanks.
[08:22] Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: minor word substitutions and sentence fragments — e.g., 'p95 tail latency' transcribed as 'pee ninety-five' in places; speaker labels sometimes shortened.
